_note: Manual-add intake. Official release URLs (justice.gov) with the release's own wording copied verbatim (excerpt limited to the named defendants). Ingested by scripts/harvest-gov.mjs through the same parse/build path as the DOJ API. 'seat' sets the district map pin when the URL has none (OPA). Optional 'names': the defendants to list, each copied exactly as the teaser spells it (used instead of the name parser; nobody else in the excerpt becomes a row). Optional 'stage' is the release's own stage (Charged, Pleaded guilty, Sentenced, Civil settlement ...); it is copied, never upgraded. Optional 'voting': true files the row as an election case (voting=true, origin 'Voting / elections'), used for official voting releases cross-posted from Invasion Update (Krennic 2026-10-20).

releases.title: EDNC Unveils Ten Federal Indictments Alleging Noncitizens Voted in the 2024 Election
releases.teaser: RALEIGH, N.C. – Today, Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, announced that a federal grand jury indicted 10 noncitizens, including an illegal alien, for illegally voting in the 2024 elections under 18 U.S.C. 611 and 1015. The grand jury returned indictments against the following individuals: Eduardd Omar Majano Sosa, 22, a native of El Salvador and an illegal alien living in Cumberland County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Gjina Gojcaj McDonald, 60, a native of the former Yugoslavia and a lawful permanent resident residing in Robeson County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. James Edward Herrmann, 47, a native of Germany and a lawful permanent resident residing in Cumberland County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Karl Fout, 73, a native of Germany and a lawful permanent resident residing in Cumberland County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Lawton Caswell McKenzie, 46, a native of Jamaica and a lawful permanent resident residing in Wayne County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Lionel Paul, 62, a native of Haiti and a lawful permanent resident residing in Granville County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Ludgardys Olena Matthews, 62, a native of Panama and a lawful permanent resident residing in Cumberland County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Mervin Sylvester Bogle, 60, a native of Jamaica and a lawful permanent resident residing in Harnett County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote. Ramona Abreu-Exia, 71, a native of Germany and a lawful permanent resident residing in Cumberland County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. Robert Harold Corbett, 69, a native of Canada and a lawful permanent resident residing in Wake County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. An indictment is merely an accusation.

releases.title: Five Non-Citizens Arrested for Voter Fraud Across the Northern District
releases.teaser: On October 13 and 14, 2026, Vikki Bradt, age 51, a British National, of Ballston Spa, NY, Samantha Merkle, age 55, a British National of Glens Falls, NY, Suad Sasic, age 30, a Bosnian National of Clifton Park, NY, Jacques Patry, age 64, a Canadian National of Tupper Lake, NY, and Paula Stitt, age 57, a Canadian National of Albany, NY, appeared on charges of voting by aliens. All defendants are lawful permanent residents. The complaints against all five defendants allege that they are aliens, who knew they were not United States citizens and that they knowingly voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for President, Vice President, Member of the United States Senate, or Member of the United States House of Representatives. The charges in the complaints are merely accusations.

releases.title: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 16 Aliens for Illegal Voting
releases.teaser: District of Idaho: Canadian national, Taralynn Bosco, 48, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegal voting by alien. Bosco allegedly voted in the 2022 general election even though she was not a United States citizen.

releases.title: Two Plead Guilty to Unemployment Insurance Benefits Fraud Conspiracy
releases.teaser: SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Las Vegas residents Ricky Lee Ware, 43, and Kimberly Ann Wallace, 30, pleaded guilty today to conspiracy to commit access device fraud, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, between July 2020 and January 2021, the defendants conspired to obtain debit cards that allowed them to access unemployment benefits. The unemployment benefits were in the names of people who did not know the defendants. The defendants then used the debit cards to withdraw more than $900,000 in unemployment benefits from ATMs. Ware and Wallace are scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins on Feb. 19, 2027, and face a maximum of 7.5 years in prison. The third defendant in the case, Carlos Lee Sanchez Jr., 46, of Sacramento, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit access device fraud in June 2026 and is scheduled to be sentenced Nov. 13, 2026. This effort is part of a California COVID-19 Fraud Enforcement Strike Force operation.

releases.title: Justice Department Charges 28 Foreign Nationals in California for Election Crimes
releases.teaser: Federal law enforcement throughout California today arrested 11 foreign nationals living in the United States who are among 28 total charged in criminal complaints with federal crimes, including that they fraudulently registered to vote in U.S. elections, electoral contests in which most of them cast illegal and fraudulently obtained ballots. Today’s arrests are part of “Operation Protect the Vote” – a coordinated effort among all four California-based United States Attorney’s Offices to combat and root out fraud in U.S. elections and protect electoral integrity. All 28 foreign nationals charged are lawful permanent residents (LPRs), or “green card” holders. Although LPRs have legal immigration status in the United States, they are not U.S. citizens and are not permitted to vote in U.S. elections. The criminal charges include making false statements in a naturalization application and some of the defendants also are charged with fraudulent voter registration. Both charges are felonies that carry a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison. Broken down by jurisdiction, the following defendants are charged in today’s takedown: Central District of California All the following defendants below in this jurisdiction face felony charges, including false statements in a naturalization application: Omar Alexander Muñoz, 72, a Belizean national living in Commerce, California, fraudulently registered to vote in September 2019, claiming his was a U.S. citizen, then voted in U.S. elections in 2020, twice in 2022, and in 2024. He also lied on his application to become a naturalized U.S. citizen when he falsely stated under oath to have never claimed to be a U.S. citizen. Amandeep Kaur, 30, an Indian national living in Rancho Palos Verdes, California, and who is seeking to become a U.S. citizen, fraudulently registered to vote in December 2022 and voted in the November 2024 U.S. election. Ana Domínguez, 60, a Salvadoran national living in Long Beach, California, fraudulently registered to vote in July 2006 and lied in her naturalization paperwork in March 2026. Axel Giovani Prera García, 46, a Guatemalan national and Pico Rivera, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2002 and 2005, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in June 2025. Flavio Alejandro Zúñiga, 43, a Mexico national and La Puente, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2003 and lied in his naturalization paperwork in February 2026. Butleng Taing, 43, a Cambodian national living in Long Beach, fraudulently registered to vote in July 2021, voted in the 2022 and 2024 U.S. elections, and lied on his naturalization paperwork in August 2025. Carlos Antonio Galeas, 54, a Honduran national and West Covina, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2012 and 2016, then lied in his naturalization paperwork in September 2018. Ernest Gutiérrez Ruvalcaba, 57, a Mexican national living in Wilmington, California, fraudulently registered to vote in February 2024 and voted one month later. Jesús Narez-Madrigal, 52, a Mexican national living in Carson, California, fraudulently registered to vote in 2014, voted in the 2024 U.S. general election, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in June 2024. José Antonio Bañuelos-Díaz, 42, a Mexican national and West Adams, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2007 and lied on his naturalization paperwork in March 2025. Muhammad Khan, 50, a Pakistani national and Anaheim, California, resident, submitted a provisional ballot in 2020 and lied on his naturalization paperwork five years later. Rouzbeh Seyamaknejad, 63, a Canadian national and Rancho Palos Verdes, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in December 2018, lied in his naturalization application in January 2024, and voted in the November 2024 U.S. election. Sulema de León, 35, a Mexican national and Long Beach, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2013, lied on her naturalization application in 2019, and voted in the November 2020 U.S. general election. Eastern District of California The following defendants are charged with voting by an alien in a federal election, a misdemeanor that carries a statutory maximum sentence of one year in federal prison: Maricela Nazarín González, 43, a Mexican national living in Clovis, California, registered to vote in 2020, indicating that she was a U.S. citizen, and voted in elections in 2022, twice in 2024, and 2025. Rony de Jesús Sicaja, 38, a Guatemalan national living in Fresno, California, fraudulently registered to vote in 2017, and voted in the June 2022 primary election and the November 2024 general election in the United States. Camino Giles Jiménez, 51, a Mexican national living in Kerman, California, knowingly voted in three U.S. elections despite knowing he is a noncitizen, the most recent election being the June 2026 primary. Juan Antonio Rivas García, 46, a Mexican national and Sacramento, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2018 and 2020, both times falsely asserting under oath that he was a U.S. citizen. Rivas voted in the 2022 and 2024 U.S. elections. Giezell Viduya Adawag, 41, a Philippines national and Vacaville, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote the day of the November 2024 general election, falsely certified that she was a U.S. citizen, and voted in the election that day. Kamlesh Navnitlal Shah, 67, an Indian national living in Sacramento, California, fraudulently registered to vote on the day of the November 2024 general election and voted that day. He is charged via information. Northern District of California The following defendants are charged with attempted procurement of naturalization contrary to law, false statement under oath in any matter relating to naturalization or citizenship, and voting by an alien: Verónica Bullene, 43, a.k.a. “Verónica Hernández Martínez,” a Mexican national living in Petaluma, California, made false statements on her naturalization application that she had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen when, in fact, she did so under penalty of perjury to register to vote in 2022 and 2023 then voted in 2024. David Shapiro, 41, a Georgian national living in San Jose, California, fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and later voted in a U.S. election, and made false statements on his naturalization application that he had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen. Moe Thida Lwin, 57, a Myanmar national and Daly City, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and then proceeded to illegally vote in a U.S. citizen. She made false statements on her naturalization paperwork as well. Manakotau Mataele Finau, 61, a Tongan national and Hayward, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in the 2024 election then vote, then lied about it in naturalization paperwork. Maribel del Carmen Garcés Barriga, 62, an Ecuadoran national and San Francisco, California, resident, made false statements in her naturalization paperwork that she never claimed U.S. citizenship and had never voted in a U.S. election or had registered to vote. In fact, Garcés fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and proceeded to vote in a U.S. election. Southern District of California The following defendants are charged with false claim to citizenship to vote, unlawful attempted procurement of naturalization, and false statement under oath in matter relating to naturalization or citizenship: José Probitsado Amaro, 51, a citizen of the Philippines living in National City, California, fraudulently registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. He then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements during his naturalization interview, denying that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting his voting history. Jennifer Jung, 31, a Canadian national living in San Diego, California, fraudulently registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. She then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements during her naturalization interview, denying that she had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting her voting history. Erick Ronaldo Soto Mendizábal, 64, a citizen of Guatemala and former Oceanside, California, resident now living in Moreno Valley, California, fraudulently registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. He then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements in his naturalization application, denying that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting his voting history. Pamele Arbués Line, 56, a citizen of the Philippines living in Escondido, California, registered to vote, cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election, and made false statements in her naturalization interview, denying that she had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting her voting history. A complaint, indictment, and information merely contain accusations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

releases.title: Illegal Alien Admits to Illegally Voting in Federal Election in New Jersey
releases.teaser: Gaye Tyndale-Simpson, an illegal alien from Jamaica, pleaded guilty to one count of voting by an alien in a federal election before U.S. Magistrate Rukhsanah L. Singh in federal court in Trenton, New Jersey. According to documents filed in the case and statements made in court, Tyndale-Simpson, 55, is a citizen of Jamaica and has never been a citizen of the United States. In November 2024, Tyndale-Simpson voted in the general election that was held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of the President.

releases.title: Former Employee of State of Illinois Subcontractor Indicted for Allegedly Fraudulently Obtaining More Than $4.6 Million in Covid-Relief Benefits
releases.teaser: ANDREA WELLINGTON engaged in fraud related to the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (“PUA”) program, one of the sources of relief under the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (“CARES”) Act, according to an indictment returned in U.S. District Court in Chicago. Wellington worked as a customer service representative for a company that subcontracted with the Illinois Department of Employment Security (“IDES”). The position gave her access to the IDES PUA system, the indictment states. IDES determined the amount of each payment to be issued to PUA claimants based, in part, on the amount of income that the claimant had earned prior to the filing of their claim for PUA benefits. The more wages reported, the greater the amount of the PUA payment. The charges allege that in the fall of 2021, after Wellington had been terminated from her position with the IDES subcontractor, she and co-defendant RANDALL EASLEY accessed the IDES PUA system and fraudulently increased the wage histories of hundreds of PUA applicants, causing IDES to disburse approximately $4,680,582 in PUA payments to which the recipients were not entitled. The indictment alleges that Wellington and Easley modified the wage histories in exchange for thousands of dollars from the applicants. Wellington, 35, of Chicago, is charged with 21 counts of wire fraud, while Easley, 38, of Chicago, is charged with 14 counts of wire fraud. Wellington and Easley were arraigned in federal court on Oct. 8, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the charges.

releases.title: Two Florida defendants sentenced to prison for nearly $900,000 health care scam
releases.teaser: According to court documents, the following defendants pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit health care fraud, mail fraud, and wire fraud: Steven Anthony Churchill, 39, of Boca Raton, Florida, was sentenced to 24 months in prison; Samson Kollelil Solomon, 28, of Pompano Beach, Florida, was sentenced to 24 months in prison; and Fawn Lickteig, 46, of Lawrence, Kansas, will be sentenced on November 10, 2026. In March 2020, Steven Churchill bought Free State Pharmacy (FSP) in Lawrence, Kansas, but under the name of a now deceased, accused coconspirator. FSP operated as a mail-order pharmacy despite representing itself to Medicare as a retail pharmacy.

releases.title: Muncie Man Accused of Falsely Requesting over $1 Million in COVID-19 Relief Tax Credits
releases.teaser: Gregory Vernon Dupree, 38, of Muncie, has been charged in a federal indictment with eight counts of filing false COVID-19 claims,including claims for the Employee Retention Credit (ERC) and COVID‑related Sick and Family Leave credits. These charges were brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. According to the indictment, between January 2021 and January 2022, Dupree allegedly filed eight Forms 941 (Employer’s Quarterly Federal Tax Return) with the Internal Revenue Service. Through these filings, Dupree made claims against the United States requesting refunds totaling over $1 million, knowing those claims to be false.

releases.title: Waipahu Women Sentenced to Two Years in Prison for Pandemic and Tax Fraud While Earning Millions from an Unlicensed Construction Business
releases.teaser: Heidi Cafirma, 46, of Waipahu, Hawaii, was sentenced on September 30, 2026, by United States District Judge Shanlyn A.S. Park to 24 months in prison followed by 3 years of supervised release for filing false tax returns and wire fraud. Cafirma was also ordered to forfeit $70,500 and pay up to over $1 million in restitution, which total amount will be determined by the court at a later date. Cafirma pled guilty pursuant to a plea agreement in December 2025. In 2020, the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act created the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) unemployment insurance program to provide emergency unemployment payments to certain workers whose livelihoods were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic but who were ineligible for traditional state unemployment insurance benefits, such as business owners, self-employed workers, independent contractors, and those with a limited work history who were out of business or had significantly reduced their services as a direct result of the pandemic. To obtain either traditional unemployment insurance (UI) or PUA UI benefit payments, claimants could submit a claim online. If approved, the U.S. Treasury typically deposited payments every week into a claimant’s bank account. To continue to receive benefit payments, claimants were required to certify on a weekly basis under penalty of law that they remained unemployed or partially employed, and eligible to receive benefit payments. According to court documents, Cafirma admitted that between June 2020 and September 2021, she submitted 22 false claims online for UI benefit payments for herself by repeatedly falsely certifying under penalty of law that she was unemployed and not receiving income, despite knowing that her certifications were false because she received over $1 million in income during that period from her and her husband’s unlicensed construction business. Cafirma fraudulently obtained at least $70,500 in unemployment insurance and PUA UI benefits to which she was not entitled.

releases.title: New Haven Man Pleads Guilty to Pandemic Relief Program Fraud Offense
releases.teaser: DAVANTE MALLARD, 33, of New Haven, waived his right to be indicted and pleaded guilty today before U.S. District Judge Sarah F. Russell in New Haven to an offense stemming from a pandemic relief program fraud scheme. According to court documents and statements made in court, in March 2020, Congress passed legislation that sought to mitigate the economic harm caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Legislation included the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (the CARES Act), which created employee retention credits (ERCs) that were intended to repay employers for certain costs expended to retain employees during the pandemic and permitted businesses to recoup previously paid wages and certain health insurance costs, and the Families First Coronavirus Response Act, which created the sick and family leave credit (SFLC) that reimbursed small and mid-sized employers for the cost of providing paid sick and family leave wages to employees for leave related to COVID-19 during the pandemic. Mallard owned Mallard Dynasty Realty Group (MDR Group), which provided real estate and property management services. The business earned little to no income, had no employees, had not paid wages, and had not filed W-2 forms with the Internal Revenue Service. In early 2022, Mallard was contacted by individuals who he knew who instructed him to open an online account with a business that provided online tax preparation services. Mallard than provided the individuals with the account information and password. Between April 2022 and February 2023, the individuals accessed the account and prepared and filed with the IRS fraudulent Employer’s Quarterly Federal Tax Returns (Forms 941) for MDR Group. The Forms 941 misrepresented the number of employees and total wages paid, and were used to apply for large ERC and SFLC refunds. When contacted by the IRS to verify information about MDR Group, Mallard provided false information, including that his business had five employees. Between August 2022 and March 2023, MDR Group received from the IRS six refund checks totaling $256,906. Mallard kicked a portion of the refund monies back to the individuals who orchestrated the scheme. Mallard pleaded guilty to making false claims regarding IRS refunds, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of five years.

releases.title: Slidell Man Sentenced for Cares Act Fraud
releases.teaser: MARCEL GROSS (“GROSS”) , age 56, of Slidell, was sentenced on October 13, 2026 by U.S. District Judge Darrel James Papillion, to four years’ probation and the payment of $350,272 in restitution, for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. GROSS fraudulently obtained a Paycheck Protection Program loan, which was a form of assistance authorized by the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

releases.title: National Fraud Enforcement Division Obtains Guilty Plea of Pensacola Postal Worker for PPP Loan Fraud
releases.teaser: Dominique J. Stanberry, 33, of Pensacola, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to two counts of wire fraud involving Small Business Administration (SBA) Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan funds. This prosecution was part of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud launched by President Donald J. Trump, a whole-of-government effort to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “We saw unprecedented levels of fraud during the COVID-19 pandemic by scammers, like this defendant, who sought to enrich themselves by ripping off the American taxpayer, but my office will tirelessly pursue those fraudsters to make them pay for their crimes. Anyone in the Northern District of Florida who abuses or defrauds a Federal benefit program should be on notice: my office is coming for you.” Court documents reflect that in 2021, the defendant, while working full time as a United States Postal Service employee, caused to be submitted a fraudulent online application for a PPP loan that falsely claimed she was self-employed with a business that lost income due to the COVID-19 pandemic. As a result of her fraud, the defendant received $20,833 in PPP loan funds to which she was not entitled.

releases.title: Sanford Woman Sentenced for Theft of Government Money
releases.teaser: U.S. District Judge John A. Woodcock, Jr., sentenced Cori Godin , 47, to 18 months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. Godin was also ordered to pay $37,105 in restitution. Godin pleaded guilty on November 18, 2025. According to court records, Godin falsely claimed to be unemployed in order to receive unemployment insurance benefits, including federally funded benefits intended to address the COVID-19 pandemic. Unemployment insurance is a joint state and federal program that provides monetary benefits to eligible beneficiaries. Payments are intended to provide temporary financial assistance to lawful workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own. Beginning in about March 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, several federal programs expanded unemployment insurance eligibility and benefits. For a period of approximately 13 months in 2020 and 2021, Godin falsely claimed to be unemployed and received approximately $37,105 in benefits.

releases.title: Texas residents charged with promoting Illegal tax shelter
releases.teaser: a federal grand jury in Dallas, Texas returned an indictment on Sept. 22, 2026, charging four Texas residents with conspiracy to defraud the United States and other crimes for promoting an illegal tax shelter. According to the indictment, Texas residents Duncan John MacDonald, Sarah Duren, Richard Ronald Cayce and Thomas Weickgenant promoted and sold a fraudulent trust scheme that was used to shelter more than $1.5 billion of income, causing an estimated tax loss to the IRS of more than $200 million.

releases.title: Somerset Lifesciences Inc. Agrees to Pay $4M to Resolve Allegations of Causing Medicare to Pay Claims for its Mislabeled Generic Drug
releases.teaser: Somerset Lifesciences Inc. (Somerset) has agreed to pay $4 million to resolve common law claims for causing Medicare Part D (Medicare) to pay for its prescription-only (Rx-only) generic drug Olopatadine when it was no longer eligible for Medicare coverage. Medicare does not cover drugs that can be purchased by retail customers over-the-counter (OTC) without a prescription. In 2020, the brand name version of Olopatadine switched from Rx-only to OTC, and Somerset was required to change Olopatadine’s label from Rx-only to OTC as well. Instead, Somerset continued to label and sell Olopatadine as Rx-only and caused Medicare to wrongfully pay claims for an OTC drug.
releases.stage: Civil settlement (allegations only, no determination of liability)

releases.title: Negril Agrees to Settle Allegations of Improper Medicaid Billing
releases.teaser: To resolve allegations that Negril Incorporated and its owners violated the False Claims Act and the Virginia Fraud Against Taxpayers Act by causing false claims to be submitted to the Virginia Medicaid Program, the company has agreed to a $1,817,910.60 civil settlement. The Government alleged that, from January 2021 through May 2022, Negril billed Virginia Medicaid for certain mental health skill‑building services under its National Provider Identification (NPI) number. However, the company that actually provided those services to Virginia Medicaid beneficiaries did not have its own NPI, was not credentialed through the Virginia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Services and was not enrolled as a Medicaid provider. Under the parties’ billing arrangement, Negril submitted the claims to Virginia Medicaid, remitted 75 percent of the Medicaid reimbursement to the other company, and retained the remaining 25 percent.
releases.stage: Civil settlement (no admission of wrongdoing, no determination of liability)

releases.title: Dover Contractor and Owners Pay $295,204 to Settle Postal Service Overbilling Claims
releases.teaser: Garrett Mechanical Inc., a Dover repair and maintenance contractor; Hey Brother, LLC, a Florida limited liability company; Joseph Bruni; and Daniel Tulchin have agreed to pay $295,204 to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by overbilling the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) for work performed at Postal facilities. Garrett Mechanical Inc., owned and operated by Bruni, began providing repair and maintenance services at USPS facilities in February 2021. In May 2022, Hey Brother, owned by Tulchin, purchased substantially all of Garrett Mechanical Inc.’s assets. Following the sale, Bruni continued to work for Hey Brother, which did business as Garrett Mechanical, and reported to Tulchin. The companies performed work for USPS until September 2023 and billed USPS approximately $263,576 between 2021 and 2023. As part of the settlement, the defendants admitted that from February 2021 through September 2023, the companies submitted claims to USPS that included inflated labor hours, inflated material costs, false completion certificates, and forged signatures of USPS employees. As a result, USPS paid the companies more than it owed under the service agreement.

releases.title: Wyoming County Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Immigration Fraud
releases.teaser: Peggy Jill Hendrick, 58, of Pineville, pleaded guilty today to fraud and misuse of visas, permits, and other documents. Hendrick admitted that she falsified employee eligibility verification forms for seven illegal aliens who worked at her restaurant. According to court documents and statements made in court, on February 18, 2026, a law enforcement officer inspected the Pineville restaurant owned by Hendrick to check if every employee had a Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification. As part of her guilty plea, Hendrick admitted that she falsely told the officer that she possessed a completed I-9 form for each employee. The officer told Hendrick that she had three business days to produce the I-9 forms for review. Hendrick admitted that following the inspection, she prepared I-9 forms for seven employees she believed were highly likely illegal aliens and not authorized to work in the United States.

releases.title: Massachusetts Man Charged for His Role in Marriage and Immigration Document Fraud
releases.teaser: A federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Jingming Chen, 31, of Quincy, Massachusetts, with Conspiracy to Commit Marriage Fraud and Immigration Document Fraud. According to allegations in the indictment, Chen, a U.S. citizen, was paid by a Chinese national co-conspirator residing in Aurora, Ohio, to enter into a sham marriage and commit immigration document fraud by fabricating evidence to support the false claim that their marriage was legitimate. They submitted false statements to the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service (USCIS) to obtain lawful permanent resident status—commonly known as a Green Card—and other immigration benefits for the co-conspirator.

releases.title: ICE HSI Arrests Non-Citizen for Illegally Voting in 2024 Election
releases.teaser: Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) arrested Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari, a non-citizen, for knowingly making a false claim of United States citizenship to vote in the 2024 general election. On September 10, a federal grand jury in the District of Minnesota returned the two-count indictment charging Chaudhari with allegedly making the false citizenship claim. According to the indictment, on or about November 5, 2024, Chaudhari signed the voter signature certificate required by Minnesota law to vote in the general election. The certificate required him to swear or affirm that he was a citizen of the United States. The indictment alleges Chaudhari was not a U.S. citizen and knowingly made the false citizenship statement in order to vote.

releases.title: DOL OIG Great Lakes Region Announces Charges and Arrests in Multiple Unemployment Insurance Fraud Schemes Tied to Gang Activity
releases.teaser: DETROIT — On October 6, 2026, Derrick Thompson, a multi-convicted felon with previous charges of fraud, assault and felony firearms violations, was arrested by DOL-OIG and ATF agents for his role in an unemployment insurance (UI) fraud scheme. Thompson was previously charged with one count of bank fraud and one count of aggravated identity theft. He is alleged to have filed dozens of UI claims in his own name and in the names of others not associated with him, defrauding various state workforce agencies (SWA) of approximately $400,000 in UI benefits.

releases.title: Federal Grand Jury Indicts Ten Foreign Nationals for Voter Fraud in Minnesota Elections
releases.teaser: The defendants and their charges include: Bhator Konah Bryant, 61, a Liberian national, on one count of making a false claim of citizenship in order to vote. She is alleged to have falsely claimed United States citizenship when registering to vote on October 18, 2024. The defendant had her initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elsa M. Bullard on September 29, 2026. Edvile Vaidoto Edmunds, 59, a Lithuanian national, on one count of voting by alien. She is alleged to have voted illegally as an alien in Minnesota on November 8, 2022. The defendant had her initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elsa M. Bullard on September 29, 2026. Joshua Frederick Kofi Edzie, 63, a Ghanaian national, on two counts of making a false claim of citizenship in order to vote and one count of voting by alien. He is alleged to have voted illegally as an alien in Minnesota on August 11, 2026, and falsely claimed United States citizenship in order to vote on October 23, 2024 and August 11, 2026. The defendant had his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elsa M. Bullard on September 28, 2026. Alan Barbu Kargbo, 48, a Liberian national, on one count of making a false claim of citizenship in order to vote and one count of voting by alien. releases.title: Four Non-Citizens Charged with Illegally Voting in 2024 Election
releases.teaser: PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that four non-citizens residing in Philadelphia have been charged with illegally voting. Under both federal and state law, only U.S. citizens may vote in Pennsylvania. Jamil Ahmad, 50, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. At that time, Ahmad was a citizen of Pakistan and a lawful permanent resident of the United States. Nighat Jamil, 47, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. Jamil is a citizen of Pakistan and a lawful permanent U.S. resident. Hacina Saadi, 48, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. Saadi is a citizen of France and an illegal alien. Paulo Silva, 54, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. Silva is a citizen of Portugal and a lawful permanent U.S. resident.

releases.title: Non-Citizens Charged with Election Crimes
releases.teaser: Jamaican national Staciann Pollion Davis, 42, a lawful permanent resident, was charged by criminal complaint with voting as an alien. Davis allegedly voted in the November 2024 general election in Clarke County, Alabama, despite not being a United States citizen. Peruvian national Silvia Delgado Phelps, 78, a lawful permanent resident, was charged by criminal complaint with voting as an alien. Phelps allegedly voted in multiple elections in Baldwin County, Alabama, despite not being a United States citizen.

releases.title: Lawful Permanent Resident from Cuba Arrested for Unlawful Voting by an Alien
releases.teaser: KANSAS CITY, Mo. – A lawful permanent resident from Cuba was arrested today after being charged with unlawful voting by an alien. Andre’s Garcia, 64, was charged with two counts of illegally voting in federal elections in November 2022 and November 2024. Garcia was born in Cuba to two Cuban citizens and immigrated to the United States during his childhood. In 2009, he applied for and was granted lawful permanent residency. Prior to even becoming a lawful permanent resident, Garcia registered to vote in Cass County, Mo. in 2004. Garcia has voted regularly for the last 20 years in at least 15 elections, including at least 13 federal elections. Lawful permanent residents are not allowed to vote in federal elections and are not allowed to vote in state or local elections in Missouri. Garcia knew he was not a United States citizen but nevertheless claimed to be one when registering to vote in 2004 and again in 2013.

nationality.Andre’s Garcia: A lawful permanent resident from Cuba

releases.title: Italian Alien Charged with Voting in 2024 General Election and Lying About it
releases.teaser: Andrea Catanese (60), an Italian national, has been charged by federal indictment with voting by an alien, attempting to procure naturalization unlawfully, and making a false statement related to naturalization. If convicted on all counts, Catanese faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in federal prison. U. S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to the indictment, Catanese, voted in the 2024 general election despite not being a citizen of the United States. The indictment further alleges that afterward, Catanese falsely stated he had never voted in a federal election on an Application for Naturalization and then made the same false statement to an immigration official who was reviewing the application.

releases.title: Federal prosecutors crack down on illegal voting: Seven non-citizens charged in sweeping federal election integrity operation
releases.teaser: Helen Sayen Adams, is a 67-year-old citizen of Nigeria and lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder) since May 2024, is charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. Adams allegedly falsely claimed U.S. citizenship on a Texas Voter Registration Application in June 2024 and voted in the November 2024 general election in Tarrant County. She later admitted she was not a U.S. citizen. Joshua Nmelichukwu Akpom, is a 27-year-old citizen of Nigeria and lawful permanent resident since 2016, charged with false statements in relation to naturalization. As alleged, Akpom falsely denied on his 2026 naturalization application that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship, registered to vote, or voted, despite registering in 2017 and voting in the 2018 general election. Due to the five‑year statute of limitations, prosecutors relied on the naturalization offense rather than the voting conduct. Carlos Salas Barrios, is a 41-year-old Mexican citizen and lawful permanent resident since 2018, charged by complaint with allegedly voting by an Alien in a Federal Election. Barrios unlawfully cast a provisional ballot in Tarrant County in the November 2024 general election despite not being a U.S. citizen and not being registered. Although the ballot was ultimately rejected, casting it was still unlawful under Texas and federal law. Khalwinder Singh Bhengura, is a 69-year-old citizen of India and lawful permanent resident since 2022, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. Bhengura falsely claimed U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in January 2024 and again when applying for a Texas driver license later that year in August. He voted in the November 2024 general election and later admitted he knew he was not a citizen. He was arrested on Sept. 11. Celestin Katubadi, is a 20-year-old citizen of the Democratic Republic of Congo and lawful permanent resident, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to vote. Katubadi cast a provisional ballot in Tarrant County during the November 2024 general election after falsely claiming U.S. citizenship on an affidavit of provisional voter. Although his ballot was rejected, casting it was still unlawful Texas and federal law. Rocio Thrasher, is a 38-year-old Mexican citizen and lawful permanent resident since 2017, charged with voting by an alien in a federal election and false statement of citizenship in order to register to vote. According to the indictment, Thrasher allegedly falsely declared U.S. citizenship when registering in June 2024 and voted in the November 2024 general election. She later admitted knowing she was not a citizen.

releases.title: Three Aliens Charged with Voting in Federal Elections
releases.teaser: Pauline Lewis, 65, an alien residing in Dawsonville, Georgia, is alleged to have voted by absentee ballot in the November 5, 2024, January 5, 2021, and November 3, 2020 federal elections. Lewis is allegedly a citizen of Antigua and Barbuda who entered the United States on a student visa in 1979 and remained in the country but never applied to become a U.S. citizen. Today, she appeared in federal court following her arrest on a criminal complaint charging her with voting as a non-citizen in a federal election. Gabriel Covarrubias, 44, an alien residing in Lawrenceville, Georgia, is alleged to have voted in person using a false name in the November 5, 2024 federal election. Covarrubias is allegedly a citizen of Mexico who falsely claimed in a U.S. passport application submitted in March 2023 that he had a different name and was born in Puerto Rico. On September 1, 2026, he waived indictment and was charged by criminal information with making a false statement in a U.S. passport application and voting as a non-citizen in a federal election. Analiea Milliscent Eccles, 43, an alien residing in Morrow, Georgia, is alleged to have voted nine times between 2008 and 2024. Eccles is allegedly a citizen of Venezuela who entered the United States on a temporary visitor visa in 1991 and remained in the country, applying for and receiving Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) status in 2013. Although she allegedly sought to renew that status earlier this year, she has never applied to become a U.S. citizen. On September 14, 2026, she appeared in federal court following her arrest on a criminal complaint charging her with voting as a non-citizen in a federal election and making a false claim of U.S. citizenship to vote in an election.

releases.title: Alien Charged with Illegally Voting in Federal Election and Making False Statements While Applying for U.S. Citizenship
releases.teaser: According to the criminal complaint, Sanata Coulibaly, 64, of Hudson County was a non-citizen when she registered to vote via a paper application at the Office of the Hudson County Superintendent of Elections. On her voter registration form she falsely certified and attested that she was a United States citizen. In order to register, and to vote in federal elections, a person must be a United States citizen. According to the criminal complaint, Coulibaly cast ballots in the November 2018 mid-term election, the July 2020 primary election, the November 2020 general election, and the 2024 general election. Each of those elections included candidates who were vying for election to federal offices. At the time she cast her ballots, Coulibaly, who entered the United States from Senegal on a B-1 nonimmigration visa, was not a United States citizen and was therefore not authorized to vote in federal elections.

releases.title: Colombian national sentenced for stealing U.S. citizen’s identity to vote; obtain citizenship, passport
releases.teaser: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — An HSI investigation resulted in a three-year federal prison sentence for criminal illegal alien Carlos Felipe Jaramillo Grajales. The 55-year-old Colombian criminal illegal alien, residing in Jacksonville, was convicted for using the identity of a U.S. citizen to obtain government-issued documents and vote unlawfully in federal elections . Jaramillo was sentenced for making false statements in an application for a U.S. passport, aggravated identity theft, falsely claiming that a Social Security number had been assigned to him, and falsely claiming eligibility to vote in an election . The court also entered a judicial order for Jaramillo’s removal to Colombia. According to court documents, Jaramillo used the name, date of birth and Social Security number of a U.S. citizen to apply for and obtain a U.S. passport. He used the same stolen identity information to obtain and repeatedly renew a Florida driver’s license, register to vote, and vote in several elections. “This criminal illegal alien spent years exploiting a stolen identity of a United States citizen to obtain government documents, claim benefits, and unlawfully participate in the electoral process,” said HSI Jacksonville Assistant Special Agent in Charge Tim Hemker. “This conviction demonstrates that identity theft, immigration fraud, and fraud against the integrity of United States government systems will be investigated thoroughly and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. HSI remains committed to protecting victims, safeguarding public institutions, and ensuring that those who abuse our immigration and identification systems are held accountable.” Jaramillo first obtained a Florida driver’s license in the victim’s name in March 2003 and renewed it several times, most recently in February 2024. In April 2003, he applied for a passport using the victim’s identity and provided a Puerto Rican birth certificate in the victim’s name, along with the fraudulently obtained driver’s license. Based on those documents, he was issued a passport in May 2003. He later submitted passport renewal applications in February 2013 and March 2023, receiving renewed passports each time. In December 2010, Jaramillo submitted a Florida voter registration application using the stolen identity and falsely affirming that he was a U.S. citizen born in Puerto Rico. His voter registration was approved, and he subsequently voted in several elections, including the election held in Duval County on Nov. 3, 2020.
